simple.meaning: גָּלַם (gâlam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to fold.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 2 Kings, beginning at 2 Kings 2:8. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּלַם (H1563) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּלַם (gâlam) / H1563 is traced through 2 Kings 2:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1563. galam [ גָּלַם ] verb wrap up, fold, fold together (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic in derivatives) — Qal Imperfect וַיִּגְלֹם 2Kin 2:8 וַיִּגְלֹם אֶתאַֿדַּרְתּוֺ אֵלִיָּהוּ וַיִּקַּח .

occurrences.englishText: Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters, and they were divided here and there, so that they both went over on dry ground.
